class.name: WeatherSkyMaterial
class.brief_description: A physical sky with volumetric clouds from the weather map.
class.description: Godot's [PhysicalSkyMaterial] atmosphere with clouds raymarched through it, after Guerrilla's Nubis and Frostbite: a layer on a round planet, Beer-Lambert steps that conserve energy, a forward and a back Henyey-Greenstein lobe, Wrenninge's multiple scattering octaves and a two-stream diffuse term, and six steps towards the sun from each sample. The clouds are drawn in the half resolution pass, with fewer steps for the radiance map that lights the scene. A [WeatherMap3D] in the scene sends it the cloud cover, type, storms and drift at its [member WeatherMap3D.update_rate]; without one, the sky shows the defaults. Set the [Sky]'s [member Sky.process_mode] to [constant Sky.PROCESS_MODE_INCREMENTAL] or [constant Sky.PROCESS_MODE_REALTIME] so the lighting follows the moving clouds. Its uniforms are under [b]Shader Parameters[/b]: the atmosphere's (as [PhysicalSkyMaterial]), and [code]cloud_steps[/code], [code]cloud_radiance_steps[/code], [code]cloud_light_steps[/code], [code]cloud_far[/code] and [code]cloud_brightness[/code]. The [code]weather_map[/code] group is set by the map. Under path tracing, bounce rays see the clouds through the radiance map. Enable [member Environment.pathtracing_sky_shader_enabled] for camera rays to see them at full detail. [b]Note:[/b] Night skies are not handled: without a sun the clouds are dark.
